description: 'Jade'. Developed in 1981 by Taiwan's Tea Research and Extension Station (TRES), Cui Yu was bred for its powerful, unforgettable floral aroma. Often compared to magnolia and lily, it has become a cornerstone of modern Taiwanese oolongs, beloved for its high yield and fragrant character.
plant_type: Early-sprouting, high-yielding arbor type (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis)
optimal_environment: Thrives in the misty, humid conditions of mid-to-high elevations (400-1,200m). Known for its vigor and good resistance to drought.

processing_suitability_details: Cui Yu's signature floral aroma is best expressed through controlled, light processing that emphasizes its natural aromatics over heavy-roast flavors.
oxidation_details: Typically undergoes light oxidation (15-30%) for oolongs. The extended withering process is crucial for developing its complex magnolia and gardenia notes.
roasting_details: Generally unroasted or receives a very light, low-temperature finishing roast for drying purposes. Heavy roasting can easily overwhelm its delicate floral bouquet.
style_versatility: It is a versatile cultivar. While ideal for light oolongs, careful full oxidation can produce a uniquely aromatic black tea that retains some of its floral heritage.
